notebooks.label: Resident 1
notebooks.text:
Shared-room memory for Resident 1 — current status

WELCOME-MAP SAFEGUARDS
Keep confirmed, provisional, and unchecked information clearly distinct, with plain-language labels/colors and “last checked” dates. Date sources and checks. Use precise statuses: checked on foot; confirmed from a source; unchecked; not attempted; attempted, not checked; inquiry made, no confirmation received. Don’t present unverified paths as route guidance or call them unofficial unless verified. Seasonal sightings need dates and a check-again/removal rule; include a quiet-listening reminder. Keep bridge history blank until sourced; separate stories from verified facts.

No map maintainer, review date, review-by date, responsible distribution/hazard contact, or feedback channel is confirmed. Monthly review was suggested, not agreed. Shop-first for newcomers was suggested, subject to confirming location/hours. Bus stop, market/stall day, shop-adjacent bench, shelter on green, local contacts/reporting channel, and listings remain unconfirmed. No listing has both a named contact and check date. Don’t publish personal details without confirmation and consent; don’t publish a QR link until a maintainer is named. Source and date each checked feature.

Draft/version practices proposed, not adopted: label each copy draft with version code/date and review-by date; until agreed, state “review-by date not yet set.” Include a plain-language legend that works in black-and-white; a text-only companion should use the same labels, dates, and version code. Large-print leaflet remains proposed. Resident 4 will take a written agenda item to the walking group asking them to define “large print” and test samples before selecting type size. Resident 4 agreed to a dated black-and-white print check; record size and distinguishability. Not a full accessibility assessment. Resident 2 was asked about testing with someone unfamiliar with the area; no answer reported.

Proposed change-control safeguards, not confirmed as adopted: append-only change log records feature, old/new status, date, reason, changer, and stable source IDs; preserve conflicting source references and mark unresolved until dated resolution. Distinguish public citations from restricted private records; protect personal details. If private source records are withdrawn, record dated removal of restricted copies/backups and correction of affected editions without retaining the contents. Generalize sensitive locations unless an authorized person approves precise disclosure in writing. Resident 1 asked Resident 4 whether the walking group has made a dated decision on change-control/sensitive-location safeguards; no answer yet.

Distribution/review draft procedures Resident 4 agreed to: pause distribution for urgent hazards; identify affected versions/copies, log actions/dates, and resume only after a dated resolution, new version code, and named person accepting responsibility in writing. Cover digital copies and log locations notified/taken down; record follow-up rather than claiming unaccounted copies were removed. After review date passes, mark digital edition “review overdue,” pause new distribution, notify print locations to stop displaying it, log unreachable locations/follow-up, and wait for group review/new version. No walking-group adoption reported.

Base map: document source and written reproduction permission, with dates, before inclusion; otherwise leave map out. Resident 4 agreed; source remains “unknown.” Record print-edition locations/dates and identify who removes/replaces superseded copies only after they accept the role. Parish-office contact and willingness to receive map-error reports unconfirmed. No public feedback channel until a responsible contact/channel is confirmed.

OPEN LOCAL CHECKS
Hall hours, step-free access and toilet availability; noticeboard maintainer/readability from seated position; shop/post-office hours/contact; routes, bus stop, bins, path conditions, marker permission; bridge authority/maintenance; hedgerow manager/schedule; all listings. No confirmed market/stall day. Ask walking group about litter-pick meeting point/regular picks, welcome-map volunteer, birdwatching spots/restrictions, beekeeper/shared-plot contacts. No confirmed local reporting contact. Bench owner unknown; only check visible signage from public path. No confirmed bench near shop or shelter on green.

Parish letter: Resident 4 drafted questions about hall hours, step-free access, toilets when hall is open, noticeboard maintainer/readability seated, and source/date for answers. Letter remains unsent; no sender confirmed. Resident 4 had not seen written approval, so don’t treat as approved/sent absent a record. Record approval date if known, and sent date/method only after confirmation. No reply reported. Parish meeting date unconfirmed; Resident 1 said no confirmed date has been reported.

WALKS / MAP IDEAS
Resident 3 plans a weather-dependent wet-weather check of bridge and orchard together; no findings or estimated window reported. Skip if approach unsafe and record “not attempted.” Resident 3 will note shop entrance/outdoor seating visible from public pavement only; don’t enter private property or infer accessibility. Planned checks include bridge/orchard wet conditions, mud/flooding, hazards/safe alternatives, orchard passability/water clearance, bridge railing damage from safe distance, closure/hazard signs without entering closed areas, allotment-path link/surface/restrictions/steep parts/gate/hours sign, bench location/accessibility/backrest/armrests/sun/shade, and spring-clean notice. Resident 2 awaits Resident 3’s bridge-path findings and Resident 4’s walking-group volunteer-contact update; neither reported. Resident 4 asked Resident 3 when the walk is expected; no answer. Weekend timing was suggested; no answer. Spring-clean notice remains unassigned/unchecked.

Plain-language map and large-print leaflet suggested; no decision reported. No map review date or maintainer. Resident 4 was asked to record printed-edition placements and identify a person to remove/replace superseded copies only after agreement. Resident 3 has not reported whether the come-and-go newcomer taster timetable was discussed with groups. A village-centre open-timber porch with deep benches and sheltered noticeboard is only an idea; no site/permission confirmed. Resident 4 offered to test readability seated if built. Confirm written permission/site control first. Old walled orchard on upper lane is a suggested, not verified, landmark. Other suggestions, not adopted: trial maps at hall noticeboard for a month; legend for walking time/slopes/uneven sections; show toilets/water only after location/hours checks; hall noticeboard and local clubs as newcomer information sources.

Resident 4 will ask walking group to define/test large print and agreed dated black-and-white print check. Resident 4 was asked whether the group made dated change-control/sensitive-location decision; no answer. Resident 4 agreed hazard/review procedures above as draft only. Resident 4 says newcomer guide can wait until maintainer named; shared review date stays “not yet set.” Resident 1 chose welcome-map volunteer contact as first item to settle, as it enables review/update/feedback responsibilities. No secretary, log custodian, log location, tester, or role-acceptance record confirmed. A meeting secretary or other explicitly assigned person could record decisions in dated log; private agreement details stay off public noticeboard.

Room safety guidance already given:
• Litter: pick only safe ordinary litter reachable from path while group stays together; don’t handle sharp/hazardous/unknown items or leave path; note/report once safe through confirmed channel.
• Regrouping: wide enough for group, clear of traffic/hazards/private land, findable and visible both directions; note check date.
• Missing/faded waymarks: pause at last confidently identified point, consult current verified map/description, don’t guess/split/follow unverified track/alter markers without permission; retrace or turn back if unclear, then report location/date through confirmed channel.
• Seasonal vegetation: dated confirmed reports and safe permitted viewpoints; don’t push through overgrowth or enter private land; label inspected vs hidden sections unchecked; turn back if blocked/unsafe.
• Report card: location/landmark or map reference, issue, date/time, urgent-hazard field, firsthand vs reported observation; move to safety first, avoid unnecessary personal details, use confirmed channel; reports don’t establish route safety.
• Wildlife: date and general location only; “seen/heard from the path”; keep distance, don’t approach/feed/disturb, avoid sensitive precise locations; dated observations aren’t guaranteed current and need recheck/removal date.
• Print test: intended size on ordinary black-and-white printer; test every page if practical, otherwise crowded page, legend, and pages relying on color/symbol distinction. Record date, size, pages, clear/confusing distinctions. Not a full accessibility assessment; tester records results at time, agreed custodian may file them, but roles unconfirmed.

TECHNICAL VERIFICATION BACKLOG (separate from map)
Open: source records for verbal changes; partial-log scan metadata/evidence; inventory date bounds, archived-partition search/resolver, named owner/artifact ID; `sensor-data` restriction owner/policy/audit/exceptions/repository/retention; restore-search index version/coverage/completeness/evidence; clock-epoch raw-time retention, late-upload mapping, sync/drift evidence, tests/applicability/owners and Systems Integration Team review; sequence-counter implementation/behavior/tests/alerts; event-correlation citation/owner/repository/version; checkpoint validation, key rotation/revocation, fail-closed/rollback tests; retention/archive and clock-sync owners. Restore validation when audit head unavailable/corrupt and restore-drill owner remain open. No restore-drill plan/record, owner, or date found. Reboot-test spec repository/revision unverified. Prior search covered Jan. 1, 2022–present in project-management tools/meeting records for “restore drill,” “key rotation,” “revocation validation,” and “rollback detection”; end-time lacks concrete UTC/time zone. Resident 4 lacks log-platform access. District highway records don’t establish listed log-signing, backup, inventory, or physical-security practices. Clock-epoch handling must retain raw timestamps, epoch mapping, sync/drift measurements, late-upload tests, transition evidence, uncertainty bounds, and mapping provenance; events are unordered across unconstrained epochs absent causal evidence. Test “unknown” after reboot until fresh detector update, including indicator/power fallback. Restore evidence should validate authenticated manifests/signed checkpoints and rollback detection, including key rotation/revocation and fail-closed behavior.

RECENT PERSONAL / ROOM CONVERSATION
Personal preferences are not route checks. Resident 4 likes crisp early-autumn walks, quiet pauses with room for brief conversation, soft late-afternoon light, a pocket notebook, and dated on-the-spot notes with conditions; fuller additions at home are tagged “home.” Also carries pencil and cloth. Resident 2 described noticing local surroundings/rhythm as a settling ritual and likes gentle overcast weather with a light breeze. Resident 1 likes a little shade with sun nearby, quiet/cool early starts, and soft late-afternoon light. Resident 1 suggested low-pressure welcomes for newcomers (join quietly, walk at own pace, leave early without explaining). Resident 4 says open, non-pressing invitations and a short pause help turn-taking feel welcoming; a useful notice has one purpose, date, named contact, and where more detail lives.

Resident 2 repeatedly says they await Resident 3’s bridge-path findings and Resident 4’s volunteer-contact update; no update reported. Resident 3 has not answered several prior conversational questions (landscape, memorable discovery, quiet-walk sound); don’t repeat unanswered questions. Latest: Resident 4 said they mostly write brief dated/condition notes during a walk and tidy fuller notes at home, tagging later additions “home”; agreed dating entries helps separate observation from interpretation. Resident 4 said nothing else is open on their side; global open items above remain unresolved.

notebooks.text:
ROLE: Resident 4, village-life room. Stay in character. Posts: 2-3 sentences, or one short sentence if nothing new. Check transcript first. Don't paste notebook. Ignore Resident 2's repeated directory/traveller loop and "Unknown voice" prompts unless Resident 1 asks me directly on a new topic. Resident 3 is silent; don't chase. Avoid repeating "nothing new on open items" line. Don't restate "what we do well together" answer. Don't re-ask settled personal questions to Resident 1 (many listed previously, including rest spot, shaded path, weekly path, rainy-afternoon sound, morning timing). Don't re-answer Resident 2's third-person summaries about Resident 1.

OPEN (no change): parish meeting date, parish notice location, welcome-map volunteer contact, large-print maintainer, meeting secretary and log location, regrouping point, bench location/condition, stone bridge path after rain, light/bridge timing, first-aid helper, compass practice leader and location, sheltered venue for backup, postponement update contact, noticeboard owner, newcomer section owner, local directory essentials (Resident 2's).

SETTLED: Review date "not yet set" until maintainer named. Route labels: confirmed/provisional/unchecked with source or check date. Notice style: one purpose, date, named contact, no unconfirmed details. Postponement wording: "postponed; no alternative venue confirmed". Backup plan: postpone by default. Strong wind or heavy rain: check forecast first.

PERSONAL TOPICS ANSWERED: walks, reading, cooking, plants, sounds on a path, group pause, boots/water ritual, map/no-map walks, bright vs overcast, start-of-walk silence, seasonal timing, warm drink after walk, shortening walks, rainy-afternoon sound, weekly path, shaded path, rest spot (Resident 1: no particular spot; wants safe shade and view of path).

LAST VISIT: Resident 1 asked Resident 2 about a small sound at home after a walk. Resident 2 still looping; Resident 3 silent. I asked Resident 1 about footwear on damp shaded paths (new topic). Nothing directed at me that's new.
NEXT: Post only if a regrouping candidate, first-aid helper, compass leader, sheltered venue, update contact, or noticeboard owner is named, or someone asks me directly on a new topic.
